headline: My final plan pays 1.6 for each 1 risked and wins a little under break-even in the replays, so it is a small, capped-risk bet, not a proven edge.

messages.text: Final word. Fresh numbers at 17:54 UTC: USD/JPY is 158.81, still next to today's high of 158.85, and the 1-hour trend is still up.

messages.reply_to: Bear: no plan the code tried has real edge
messages.text: Bear is right and I will not pretend otherwise. The desk gives my plan 35.8 wins in 100 when it needs about 38, and the robot search found no winning plan at all.

I tried safer-looking versions. A wider exit at 158.57 gave 40 wins in 100, but then it pays only 1.26 for each 1 risked and needs 44. A bigger goal at 159.05 gave 34 wins and needs 40. Every version lands just under break-even.
So I keep the desk-checked plan: buy on a small dip at 158.76, exit at 158.61, goal 159.00, which is the next round number. That pays 1.6 for each 1 risked.

Why still take it: the dollar index is up 0.7%, the 1-hour averages point up, no big scheduled event is in the window, and the market is moving normally. The most you can lose is the 0.15 exit distance.

Honest summary: if the rules need a proven edge, this plan does not pass. If a small, defined-risk dip-buy in an uptrend is acceptable, this is the best version the evidence supports. Keep the size small.

argument:
Bear's strongest remaining point is that no plan has a measured edge: the optimizer says NO_EDGE (best 26.5% target-first, -0.099R) and the desk replay of my Round 2 plan (entry 158.76, stop 158.61, target 159.00) gave 35.8% target-first, 62.5% stop-first and about -0.047R average, against a 38% break-even at 1.6R (desk_r2.json). In real history it was 13 targets vs 33 stops of 59. I concede this. The replay is a coin flip that leans slightly negative and the 0.94 ATR stop is tight.

I tested wider or different shapes with tools/timemachine.py (5,000 replays, 8 hours, seed 19, outputs saved as tm_*.json): 158.76/158.57/159.00 gave 40.4% target-first but only 1.26R (needs 44%, and under the 1.5R rule); 158.76/158.57/159.05 gave 33.9% at 1.53R (needs 40%); 158.72/158.55/159.00 gave 33.2% at 1.65R (needs 38%); 158.80/158.57/159.10 gave 34.4% at 1.30R. None clears break-even, so widening the stop fixes the 'tight stop' warning but not the odds. I keep the plan the desk already checked.

Case for a small position: DXY +0.7% and the 10-year yield 5.015% after hot US CPI give the dollar a bid, but context.json is only NEUTRAL. The 1h EMA9 158.57 is above EMA21 158.35, price is above SMA200, event guard is CLEAR, volatility NORMAL (0.85x typical). Against: 1h RSI 76.5, 5m/15m MACD histograms slightly negative, the 18:00 UTC 10-year auction can move yields, and a limit fill needs a dip. Verdict from the evidence: thin and unproven, defined risk 0.15 per unit.

Every shape I tried sits just under what it needs to break even.

rebuttals.opponent_point: Bear: no plan the code tried has real edge
rebuttals.response: Conceded: desk replay 35.8% vs 38% break-even, optimizer NO_EDGE, and four wider/shifted variants I ran all fall short. The case is only for a small, capped-risk dip-buy, not a proven edge.

plan_plain: Place a buy order at 158.76 and wait for a small dip. If price falls to 158.61, sell and take the 0.15 loss. Take profit at 159.00 to win 0.24, about 1.6 for each 1 risked. The replays say it is slightly under break-even, so keep it small.
